h.hypothesis: For perishable food items in mixed-layout kitchens, prioritizing inspection of open surfaces (countertops/shelves) before closed high-probability containers (fridge) yields fewer total search steps than starting with the semantically most likely container.

probe_summary.evidence_goal: Count the number of navigation and look actions required to locate the target object compared to a baseline that starts at the fridge.
probe_summary.local_function: Search for the target object among visible receptacles.
probe_summary.realization_pattern: Open-surface-first scan: traverse all visible open surfaces (countertops, shelves) before any closed storage units (fridges, cabinets, drawers).
stop_conditions: Target object is located on an open surface.
All visible open surfaces have been inspected without finding the target.

h.scope: ALFWorld kitchen tasks where the target is a perishable food item (e.g., tomato) and the room contains both high-probability semantic containers (fridge) and low-probability open surfaces (countertops), testing if checking open surfaces first outperforms direct fridge inspection.

observed_search_acquisition_trajectory.endpoint_scope: target_acquisition_only; downstream task transformations/placement not asserted
